title: Deck equivariance forced by naturality and diagonal normalization
statement: Let V be a nonempty connected scheme, ell a prime, P a finite group, and c:Y to V a finite etale ULift(P)-torsor with nonempty connected total space [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-torsor-section-representation]. Let F be a sheaf of ULift(Z/ell)-modules and A such a module, with inverse image c*F isomorphic to the constant sheaf of value A [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Suppose linear maps beta_W from F(W) to locally constant F(Y)-valued functions on W times_V Y commute pointwise with every morphism of etale V-objects via sectionRestriction and satisfy beta_Y(s)(Delta(y))=s for every s in F(Y) and y in Y. Then for every W, s in F(W), g in P and x in W times_V Y, beta_W(s)(sectionAction(W,g)(x)) equals sectionRepresentation(ell,F)(g)(beta_W(s)(x)).

source.place: Tags 0DV5 (3), 0DV6 and 0A3R, proof identifying the restricted representation; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS (gluing sheaves and mapping property), with module operations as in 0DV5 (3); explicit section-evaluation implementation of the fixed-torsor argument; sites.tex Example constant-sheaf (sheafification); local-section argument, extending from finite coefficients to arbitrary modules already trivialized on this fixed cover

proof.text: Put U=W times_V Y, t=p_U*s, and let f be beta_U(t) evaluated on the graph of q_U:U to Y. The open fibre O of f through x contains x and has constant value a=f(x). Regard O as an etale V-object T, with maps p:T to W and q:T to Y. Naturality identifies the graph evaluation of p*s with the constant function a. Naturality and diagonal normalization give the same graph evaluation for q*a. Injectivity in ordinaryGraphEvaluation_bijective [lem-weil-pbc-torsor-normalized-graph-evaluation] gives p*s=q*a. This produces the required local presentation using existing graph coordinates, without any new local-presentation theorem.

The proved private helper evaluation_of_local_presentation applies naturality along p and q at the graph of q, and then diagonal normalization at q(y). Pullback.hom_ext and the two projection identities identify the relevant points. Thus beta_W(s)(x)=a. This calculation uses no constant-trivialization hypothesis.

Replace q by q composed with sectionDeck(g), and a by b=F(sectionDeck(g inverse))(a). The deck identity sectionDeck(g) composed with sectionDeck(g inverse)=identity follows from mul_smul and one_smul. Contravariant functoriality therefore gives p*s=q_prime*b. The pullback projection identities show that the new lifted point is sectionAction(g)(x). Apply the proved local-evaluation helper again to obtain beta_W(s)(g*x)=b. By definition of sectionRepresentation, b is rho(g)(a), proving the assertion. Empty W has no x; the open fibre through an existing x is nonempty, and zero coefficients or the trivial group satisfy the same identities.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.GaloisCover.ordinarySectionEvaluation_equivariant
    {V : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace V] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (P : Type u) [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V) [ConnectedSpace c.P]
    (F : Sheaf V.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))))
    (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))
    (h : Nonempty ((c.π)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))].obj F ≅
      (constantSheaf c.P.smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))).obj A))
    (β : ∀ W : V.Etaleᵒᵖ, F.obj.obj W →ₗ[ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)]
      LocallyConstant (c.sectionSpace W.unop) (F.obj.obj (op c.sectionObject)))
    (hβ : ∀ (W W' : V.Etaleᵒᵖ) (f : W ⟶ W') (s : F.obj.obj W)
        (x : c.sectionSpace W'.unop),
      β W' (F.obj.map f s) x = β W s (c.sectionRestriction f.unop x))
    (hΔ : ∀ (s : F.obj.obj (op c.sectionObject)) (y : c.P),
      β (op c.sectionObject) s
        (pullback.lift (f := c.π) (g := c.π) (𝟙 c.P) (𝟙 c.P) (by simp) y) = s) :
    ∀ (W : V.Etaleᵒᵖ) (s : F.obj.obj W) (g : P) (x : c.sectionSpace W.unop),
      β W s (c.sectionAction W.unop g x) =
        (c.sectionRepresentation ℓ F).ρ g (β W s x)
